title: api: versioned request/response schema v2 - deprecations, beta headers & backward-compat shims
author: Ava Chen
description: Context: The API surface continues to evolve to support structured outputs, function/tool calling, and clearer upgrade paths for clients. This PR introduces a new 'v2' request/response schema that formalizes recent OpenAI-compatibility enhancements (structured output shape, explicit tool call metadata) while providing runtime compatibility shims and deprecation headers to avoid breaking existing clients. Motivation: we need a stable upgrade path for customers using older SDKs and third-party OpenAI-compatible code while enabling new features behind an opt-in beta header. Changes: 1) Add support for Accept-API-Version / X-Redwood-Api-Version headers with 'v2' semantics; 2) Introduce 'response_schema' top-level field in v2 responses and a canonical 'tools' metadata block for function calling; 3) Emit 'X-Redwood-Deprecation' and 'X-Redwood-Deprecation-Notice' headers on deprecated fields when accessed by older schema versions; 4) Ship backward-compat shims in the HTTP gateway to translate v2 responses to v1 shape for clients that do not send the beta header; 5) Add runtime feature-flag to toggle strict validation and small e2e test harness. Migration: clients can opt into v2 by sending Accept-API-Version: v2 or X-Redwood-Api-Version: v2; SDK updates will default to v1 for now but include a simple opt-in toggle. Rollout: staged rollout via canary on 10% of traffic, monitoring for regression in downstream SDKs and OpenAI-compatible adapters. Testing: unit tests for schema translation, integration tests for streaming responses & function call roundtrips, manual verification against redwood-openai-compat suite. This PR includes docs and release notes, deprecation messaging, and a rollback plan (feature-flag + gateway rewriter reverse).
commits: add header parsing and router support for Accept-API-Version
implement v2 response_schema and tools metadata
add deprecation header emission and notice text
docs: migration guide and changelog entry
review_comments: Marco Ruiz (reviewer): Please ensure the deprecation header includes epoch timestamp and suggested migration URL. Author: Added X-Redwood-Deprecation and X-Redwood-Deprecation-Notice with timestamp and URL in translator.go.

Emily Nguyen (reviewer): The gateway shim looks heavy; can we keep translation stateless? Author: Refactored translator to be stateless per-request and added micro-benchmarks showing sub-1ms overhead per request.

Jordan Brooks (reviewer): Need an e2e test for streaming + function call when v1 client hits v2 model. Author: Added integration test that simulates streaming chunked responses and validates tool call metadata translation.
merge_outcome: merged via squash by Sanjay Patel; merge commit message: "api: schema v2 + compatibility shims (ENG-4121)"
release_notes: - Introduces v2 API schema: structured 'response_schema' and canonical 'tools' metadata; opt-in via Accept-API-Version/X-Redwood-Api-Version headers.;- Gateway now emits X-Redwood-Deprecation and X-Redwood-Deprecation-Notice headers when deprecated fields are used.;- Backward-compatibility shims translate v2 responses to v1 shape for non-opted-in clients.;- SDKs will remain v1 by default; migration guide and examples added to docs/api/versioning.md.;- Breaking change: servers will start emitting deprecation headers; behavior change behind feature-flag for strict validation.
notes_for_ops: Rollout plan: canary at 10% for 24h, monitor metrics: error_rate, schema_translation_latency, sdk_compat_errors; rollback: flip feature flag or disable gateway shim; contact on-call: infra-oncall@redwood.ai
